To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the water potential of the leaves of the mature wheat leaves is similar to that of nutrient medium, (ii) nitrate uptake from the medium is stimulated by short-term water stress, (iii) the rate of nitrite accumulation in the leaves is not changed, and (iv) the nitrate pool in the leaves is increased by short-term water deficit.
the water potential of the leaf is maintained at the threshold level of – 0.80 MPa, and the nitrate uptake is enhanced in the presence of PEG.
the water potential of mature leaves is similar to that of medium down to –0.8 MP, and is maintained at this level despite the fact that the external water potential is much lower.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a short-term effect of osmotic stress on nitrate utilization.
the effect of short-term drought stress on wheat plants with respect to nitrite uptake and reduction, and with the possible role of NO3– as an osmoticium.
the response of wheat seedlings, with particular emphasis on the nitrate utilization, to short‐term water stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
short‐term changes in the medium water potential have no influence on the nitrate reductases activity, but they affect the net nitrate uptake and the distribution of nitrate in the plant.

short‐term drought‐induced stress in wheat plants results in a decrease of the water potential in the shoot, a decrease of transpiration, an increase of nitrate uptake and accumulation, a decrease of nitrate reduction, a decrease of in vitro nitrate‐reductase activity, and a decrease in the growth of the youngest leaf.
the effect of drought on nitrate metabolism is not as simple as it is usually assumed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitrate uptake is stimulated by short-term water stress in wheat seedling, and the nitrate reduction is not affected.
the short‐term drought induced a stimulation in nitrate uptake and accumulation in the shoot.
nitrate uptake and utilization by wheat seedlings is affected by the water potential of the medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nitrate uptake is not inhibited by short-term drought stress.
nitrate uptake is stimulated by water deficit.
the water potential of the leaves is maintained at a level similar to that of mature leaves.
